newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end mostly lower.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures finished another volatile session mostly lower, but were barely fazed by the first part of the quarterly expiration.
March S&P 500s expired at the close today and are settled based on the opening of the index Friday. Other March futures and options contracts expire at the close Friday.

"If there were imbalances, I wasn't aware of them," said one S&P 500 trader on the floor of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, referring to order imbalances related to expiration published by the New York Stock Exchange in the last half-hour of the session.

Weakness in the bond market during the morning weighed on index futures, which set session lows early in the day and then recovered, only to trade in a wide choppy band in late morning and afternoon dealings, traders said.
Support remained intact near 779.00 in the June S&P 500 contract, representing a 10-month uptrend line, some traders noted.
Futures recovered in afternoon activity, reaching a new daily high, but followthrough buying failed to emerge and selling surfaced again late that pushed contracts lower.
Traders noted that overall open interest in S&P futures was somewhat low, although March open interest remained high as there was little rolling of March positions into June.

Open interest in all contracts has been typically around 250,000 at the end of a quarter, said Kevin O'Brien, stock index analyst at Prudential Securities. At this expiration it totaled about 225,000, meaning that after expiration, with the small roll, open interest would probably decline to about 175,000 contracts.
Nikkei 225 stock index futures also firmed in afternoon dealings but came under pressure by the close.

At settlement, June S&P 500s were off 3.85 points at 788.40, Nasdaq 100s were 9.25 higher at 832.75, Russell 2000s were up 3.10 points to 356.40, KCBT Value Line futures were down 0.10 points to 707.40, Nikkei 225 index futures fell 95.0 to 18,430.0 and Midcap 400s rose 2.05 points to 262.60.
